summary: An ask sits inside a point and the point closes on a belief or an image.
realLife: New Mexico's governor put an ask to the legislature in ten of sixteen points and ended each on a value or a picture.
sources: docs/story/research/address-moves.md (Elections lane, Nov 24, 2026: 6 inaugurals and 6 State of the State addresses read whole, 175 points coded)
inGame: Section `theme` shapes stand-with-reason and creed-then-pledge put the pledge or stand inside the point, followed by a value or reason move; gated on stance-for/stance-against and law-in-force/law-not-in-force.

turns.what: The point ends on the ask, with no belief after it.
turns.pulledBy: a blunt or urgent speaker; the law not in force
turns.writesBack: The ask is the last thing heard, so the reply in the talk answers it directly.

turns.what: The ask is implied by the stand and never stated.
turns.pulledBy: stance without a law in play
turns.writesBack: Nobody can later hold the speaker to a named ask.
